headline: South Korea's National Fire Research Institute says a soft, air-driven vine robot built with KAIST scouted the inside of a battery warehouse after a fire in August without pressing on the stored batteries.
score_reason: Pool 4 kept: first announced on 11 Oct 2026, inside the window, and the article matches the headline; the account is the institute's own.
importance_line: A lightweight robot was used inside a damaged battery warehouse that heavier machines could have set off again, which matters to firefighters and rescuers facing battery fires, but the account comes from the fire institute itself, a translation of a Korean report, with no detail on what the robot found.
source: SBS News, citing the National Fire Research Institute
summary: SBS News reports, citing an announcement by the National Fire Research Institute of Korea's National Fire Agency on 11 Oct 2026, that the institute used an ultralight vine robot made with a team at KAIST (the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology) to check the inside of a finished-goods warehouse at a primary battery plant in South Chungcheong Province after a fire in August 2026, where many of about 210,000 military battery packs were left unburned but hot and at risk of thermal runaway, in which an overheated battery sets off a chain reaction. Officials say tracked machines and four-legged robots were ruled out because their weight could press on the batteries, while the vine robot, which grows outward like a plant vine as compressed air is pumped in, could pass through narrow spaces without disturbing them; the account is the institute's own.
notes: The fulltext fetch held only the headline; the full article body was recovered from the SBS page itself (HTTP 200). SBS's English edition says the article was translated by AI. The deployment took place in August 2026 (day not stated) but this is its first public announcement found, so freshness is NEW; Korea Times carried it on 12 Oct 2026 (headline only seen).
